translation.title: Isoconazole Nitrate Cream
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for skin fungal infections — ringworm (of the hands, feet and groin), skin candidiasis and pityriasis versicolor — and for erythrasma.
translation.usage: Before applying, wash the affected area clean, then apply to the affected area twice a day. In particular, wash between the fingers and toes clean and dry them completely before applying this medicine. Continue the treatment for 2 to 3 weeks; for severe infections (especially infections of the hands or between the toes), continue for up to 4 weeks, and to prevent recurrence, continue the treatment for at least about 2 more weeks after the condition has cleared. For athlete's foot of the hands or toes, it is advisable to put this medicine on a clean piece of gauze and cover the infected area with it.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it or to imidazole derivatives, if you have an unusual skin disease, or on severely eroded (raw, oozing) areas. Before using it, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if you are breastfeeding. Do not use an occlusive dressing or wrapping unless directed by a doctor. In the case of candidiasis, do not use acidic soap. The oily ingredients used as the base of this medicine may degrade or damage latex rubber contraceptive products such as condoms, so take care to avoid contact as much as possible. This medicine is for external use only. When applying it to the face, be careful not to let it touch the eyes. Adverse reactions may occur, such as allergic skin reactions, redness (red spots), pain or blistering at the application site, commonly irritation and a burning feeling at the application site, occasionally weeping eczema, sweating, contact dermatitis, dryness and itching at the application site, and rarely swelling and skin cracks at the application site; if they occur, stop use and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
